hey anandhu! was just thinking about your situation - fresh cs grad looking for non-coding roles in bangalore/remote/kerala.

Okay for me.

nice. associate product manager and business analyst are solid starting points - you get to work with tech teams, understand the systems, but focus on strategy and problem-solving instead of implementation.

what's your salary expectation for these roles? fresh grad in bangalore could be looking at anywhere from 4-8 LPA depending on the company and your interview performance.

what number would make you excited to say yes?

4LPA
  Consider Technical Support Roles

4 LPA is realistic for entry-level non-coding roles, especially in bangalore. good to know you're open to technical support too - that's actually a great foot in the door for many cs grads who want to understand systems without building them.

technical support can lead to solutions engineering, customer success, or even product management down the line. you get to solve real customer problems and learn how products actually work in the wild.

what's drawing you toward technical support specifically? the customer interaction? troubleshooting? or just a solid starting point?
Everything

got it. you're open to the whole package - customer interaction, troubleshooting, learning how products work in the real world. that's actually a great mindset for technical support.

you'll be dealing with everything from basic how-to questions to complex technical issues, which means you'll learn the product inside out. that knowledge is gold if you want to move into product management or solutions engineering later.

so we're looking at associate product manager, business analyst, and technical support roles - all non-coding, all starting around 4 LPA, across bangalore, remote, kerala, chennai, kochi, and coimbatore.

anything else i should know about what you're looking for? any specific companies you're interested in or want to avoid?

Nothing else
